revision.text:
[[File:Bombing of Ujiyamada at Ozeko-cho.jpg|thumb|After the Ujiyamada Air Raid, Ōzeko‐chō in Ujiyamada City – {{ill|Ise Ginza Shindō Shopping District|ja|伊勢銀座新道商店街|lt=New Road|lt_ja=新道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Ginza Shindō Shopping District|qq=}} area]] [[File:Bombing of Ujiyamada Map, Shima Peninsula.png|thumb|300px|Map related to the Ujiyamada Air Raid (Wide area of the Shima Peninsula)]] [[File:Bombing of Ujiyamada Map, Central City.png|thumb|300px|Map related to the Ujiyamada Air Raid (Ujiyamada City urban area)]]
'''Ujiyamada Air Raid''' (宇治山田空襲) was an {{ill|air raid|ja|空襲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/air raid|qq=}} ({{ill|strategic bombing|ja|戦略爆撃|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/strategic bombing|qq=}}) conducted by the {{ill|United States Armed Forces|ja|アメリカ合衆国軍|lt=US military|lt_ja=アメリカ軍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/United States Armed Forces|qq=}} at the end of {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World War II|qq=}} in {{ill|1945|ja|1945|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1945|qq=}} (Showa 20) on Ujiyamada City in {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefecture|qq=}} (present-day {{ill|Ise City|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City|qq=}}). Both the Japanese authorities and the Shima Peninsula had stationed troops in anticipation that it would serve as one of the landing sites for the {{ill|United States Armed Forces|ja|アメリカ合衆国軍|lt=US military|lt_ja=アメリカ軍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/United States Armed Forces|qq=}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.asahi.com/area/mie/articles/MTW20120820251060001.html |title=朝日新聞デジタル：【６】高射砲 Ｂ２９に届かず - 三重 - 地域|access-date=2023-10-06|publisher=朝日新聞社}}</ref><ref name="mj2" />. However, contemporary Japanese press condemned the American side on the premise that the bombing was intended to dampen the fighting spirit of the Japanese people by attacking Ujiyamada, a city of national importance often referred to as the “Divine Capital.”<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tomioka-aichi.jp/isan/sensoutaiken/pdf-taiken/16-tokumei.pdf|title=16|author={{ill|Anonymous|ja|匿名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anonymous|qq=}}|publisher=ふるさと遺産を保存する会（富岡ふるさと会館）|accessdate=2014-11-29|archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2014-1129-1509-46/tomioka-aichi.jp/isan/sensoutaiken/pdf-taiken/16-tokumei.pdf|archivedate=2014-11-29}}</ref>
{{ill|January 14|ja|1月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/January 14|qq=}}’s {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Grand Shrine|qq=}}{{#tag:ref|伊勢神宮は正式名称を「神宮」と称し、皇大神宮（内宮）と豊受大神宮（外宮）の2つの正宮に別宮・摂社・末社・所管社と呼ばれる宮社が付属し、合計125社から構成される<ref>三橋（2013）：19 - 20ページ</ref><ref>JTBパブリッシング（2011）：24ページ</ref>。本文中で取り上げる神社は、須原大社を除いて伊勢神宮を構成する125社に含まれる。詳細は「{{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Grand Shrine|qq=}}」および「{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|lt=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|lt=List of the 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of the 125 Shrines of Ise|qq=}}」を参照。|group="注"}}{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|lt=Outer Shrine|lt_ja=外宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Daijingu|qq=}} was the target of the initial bombing, and thereafter the shrine suffered six large‐scale attacks that burned 50–60% of the urban area{{#tag:ref|『伊勢市史』<ref name="ih5">伊勢市 編（1968）：445ページ</ref>および『日本地誌 第13巻』の記述<ref name="nm">日本地誌研究所 編（1976）：353ページ</ref>。[[三重県庁]]ウェブサイト内では「市内の約60%を焼失」と記している<ref name="bm"/>。|group="注"}}.
== Overview == The {{ill|Shima Peninsula|ja|志摩半島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima Peninsula|qq=}} was an attractive target for the B‑29 – along with {{ill|Cape Shio|ja|潮岬|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cape Shio|qq=}} and {{ill|Omaezaki|ja|御前崎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omaezaki|qq=}} – so the B‑29 frequently traversed the skies above Ujiyamada City, which lies at the base of the Shima Peninsula<ref name="ss2">日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：202ページ</ref>. Ujiyamada City’s proximity to the open sea also made it vulnerable to attacks by {{ill|naval aircraft|ja|艦載機|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/naval aircraft|qq=}} in an urban setting<ref name="ss2"/>. According to records by Kishihara Monjirō of Miyagoto Town, from {{ill|1944|ja|1944|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1944|qq=}} (Showa 19) through {{ill|August 16|ja|8月16日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 16|qq=}}, 501 air raid alerts and 99 air raid warnings were issued<ref name="ss9"/>.
Air raid casualties numbered 101 dead and 240 injured, with 4,928 households partially or completely burned and 22 households destroyed<ref name="ym5">稲本ほか（2000）：285ページ</ref>. According to Inamoto Kisho et al. in <nowiki>『三重県の歴史』</nowiki>, although the scale of damage was smaller than that in other Mie cities such as {{ill|Tsu City|ja|津市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsu City|qq=}}, {{ill|Yokkaichi|ja|四日市市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokkaichi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kuwana City|ja|桑名市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwana City|qq=}}, the number of days on which air raids occurred was greater<ref name="ym5"/>.
== Conditions Prior to the Air Raid == After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji Restoration|qq=}}, the government promoted the {{ill|Shinto State Religion|ja|神道国教化|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto State Religion|qq=}}, and the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Grand Shrine|qq=}} was positioned as the highest‐Ranking {{ill|shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shrine|qq=}} in Japan<ref>新田（2014）：38ページ</ref>. With the development of modern {{ill|transportation|ja|交通機関|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/transportation|qq=}} and the linking of Ise Grand Shrine with {{ill|nationalism|ja|国家主義|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/nationalism|qq=}}, the number of pilgrims increased continuously from {{ill|1897|ja|1897|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1897|qq=}} (Meiji 30) through {{ill|1945|ja|1945|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1945|qq=}} (Showa 20)<ref name="sj">新田（2014）：39ページ</ref>. Ujiyamada City, known as the “Divine Capital”, became a magnet for people and wealth from across Japan<ref name="tm7">三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：107ページ</ref>.
In February {{ill|1933|ja|1933|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1933|qq=}} (Showa 8), the Ujiyamada City Mayor submitted an “Opinion Document Concerning the State‐Managed Special Urban Planning for the Divine Capital” addressed to the {{ill|Prime Minister|ja|Prime Minister of Japan|1=Prime Minister of Japan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prime Minister|13=User:Immanuelle/Prime Minister of Japan|qq=}} and the {{ill|Minister of Home Affairs|ja|内務大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minister of Home Affairs|qq=}}, proposing that the old downtown be redeveloped into parkland, roads, and hotel sites befitting the Divine Capital, that a new downtown be constructed in the suburbs for displaced citizens, and that a {{ill|subway|ja|地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/subway|qq=}} and an {{ill|airport|ja|空港|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/airport|qq=}} be built<ref name="tm8">三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：108ページ</ref>. In response, in {{ill|1940|ja|1940|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1940|qq=}} (Showa 15) – the year marking the {{ill|Kigenshiki 2600|ja|紀元二千六百年記念行事|lt=Emperor’s 2600th Anniversary|lt_ja=皇紀2600|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigenshiki 2600|qq=}} – the “Special Urban Planning Act for Shrine‐related Areas” was enacted<ref name="tm8"/>. Under this law, however, no new downtown was planned; only the expansion of Ise Grand Shrine’s precincts and the improvement of railways and roads were carried out<ref name="tm8"/>.
Even after the outbreak of the {{ill|Pacific War|ja|太平洋戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pacific War|qq=}}, Ise Grand Shrine remained relatively calm until around the beginning of {{ill|1943|ja|1943|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1943|qq=}} (Showa 18)<ref name="kg3">矢野（2006）：183ページ</ref>. However, from April of that year, the {{ill|permanent lantern|ja|常夜灯|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/permanent lantern|qq=}} was extinguished and air raid alerts and warnings became frequent, with pilgrims increasingly engaging in victory prayers organized by the {{ill|military|ja|軍隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/military|qq=}} and local associations ({{ill|chōnaikai|ja|町内会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/chōnaikai|qq=}})<ref name="kg3"/>. Amid these tense conditions, preparations for the scheduled {{ill|Sengu|ja|神宮式年遷宮|lt=Shrine Relocation Ceremony|lt_ja=式年遷宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengu|qq=}} in {{ill|1949|ja|1949|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1949|qq=}} (Showa 24) continued steadily<ref name="kg3"/>.
== Chronology of the Air Raid == === Damage to the Outer Shrine in the First Air Raid === [[File:Kaguraden Hall of Toyouke Grand Shrine.jpg|thumb|Outer Shrine Kaguraden (2019 [Heisei 31])]] On {{ill|January 14|ja|1月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/January 14|qq=}} {{ill|1945|ja|1945|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1945|qq=}} (Showa 20) at 2:53 p.m., a B‑29 of the {{ill|United States Armed Forces|ja|アメリカ軍|lt=US military|lt_ja=アメリカ軍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/United States Armed Forces|qq=}} attacked Ujiyamada City<ref name="ss9">日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：239ページ</ref>{{#tag:ref|Of the 62 B‑29s that bombed the {{ill|Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Nagoya Aircraft Manufacturing Works|ja|三菱重工業名古屋航空宇宙システム製作所|lt=Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Nagoya Aircraft Works|lt_ja=三菱重工業名古屋航空機製作所|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Nagoya Aircraft Manufacturing Works|qq=}}, 3 aircraft on their return flight attacked Ujiyamada City<ref name="mj1">原（1995）：57ページ</ref>.|group="注"}} – marking the first air raid on the city<ref name="ih4">伊勢市 編（1968）：444ページ</ref>. This was the first full‐scale air raid in Mie Prefecture{{#tag:ref|According to the description on the Mie Prefecture government website<ref name="bm"/>. The first air raid in Mie occurred on {{ill|April 18|ja|4月18日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/April 18|qq=}} {{ill|1942|ja|1942|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1942|qq=}} (Showa 17) – the {{ill|Doolittle Raid|ja|ドーリットル空襲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doolittle Raid|qq=}} – during which {{ill|Yokkaichi|ja|四日市市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokkaichi|qq=}} and the area of {{ill|Kuwana District|ja|桑名郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwana District|qq=}}’s {{ill|Nagashima Town (Mie)|ja|長島町|lt=Nagashima Village|lt_ja=長島村|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagashima Town (Mie)|qq=}} (present-day {{ill|Kuwana City|ja|桑名市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwana City|qq=}}) were strafed by machine guns.<ref name="group="注""/></nowiki>. In this air raid, 1 person was killed and 16 injured{{#tag:ref|According to the <nowiki>『伊勢市史』</nowiki> (see <ref name="ih4"/>) and the “History of the {{ill|Ise Police Station|ja|伊勢警察署|lt=Ise Police Station|lt_ja=宇治山田警察署|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Police Station|qq=}}”, which reports 3 severe and 14 minor injuries.|group="注"}}.
An estimated 8 bombs were dropped<ref name="ih4"/>, striking locations such as the Rensuiyama Orchard in {{ill|Tokiwacho|ja|常磐町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokiwacho|qq=}} and the northwestern end of the Nishikizuwashi Bridge in {{ill|Iwabuchi Town|ja|岩渕町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwabuchi Town|qq=}}<ref name="ss9"/>. On the Outer Shrine, 6 bombs were dropped at 5 spots, damaging the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=}}, {{ill|Kujōden|ja|九丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujōden|qq=}}, {{ill|Kaguraden|ja|神楽殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaguraden|qq=}}, and {{ill|Saikan|ja|斎館|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saikan|qq=}}<nowiki>{{#tag:ref|Gojōden and Kujōden are used for purification rituals during rain and for remote worship at subsidiary and branch shrines, Kaguraden is where invocations are held<ref>JTBパブリッシング（2011）：33, 41ページ</ref>, and Saikan is the residence for Shinto priests<ref>矢野（2006）：47ページ</ref>.|group="注"}}</nowiki>.<ref name="yk">西垣・松島（1974）：247ページ</ref>. The damage was relatively minor – limited to broken eaves, damaged shoji screens, collapsed wooden fences, and a few holes in the roofs<ref name="ah1208">{{Cite web|和書|author=中村尚徳|url=http://www.asahi.com/area/mie/articles/MTW20120818251060001.html|title=[5] Exaggerated Announcement to Boost Morale|work={{ill|Asahi Shimbun Digital|ja|朝日新聞デジタル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asahi Shimbun Digital|qq=}}|publisher={{ill|Asahi Shimbun|ja|朝日新聞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asahi Shimbun|qq=}}|date=2012-08-18|accessdate=2015-01-25|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150125095304/http://www.asahi.com/area/mie/articles/MTW20120818251060001.html|archivedate=2015-01-25}}</ref>. The shrine interpreted this as a “divine phenomenon”<ref name="kg3"/>. However, 4½ hours later on {{ill|radio|ja|ラジオ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/radio|qq=}}, the {{ill|Imperial Headquarters Announcement|ja|大本営発表|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Headquarters Announcement|qq=}} reported that “the enemy dropped several bombs in the Toyouke Grand Shrine area, causing two Saikan and five Kaguraden structures to collapse”<ref name="yk"/>. In response, the {{ill|newspaper|ja|新聞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/newspaper|qq=}} on {{ill|January 15|ja|1月15日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/January 15|qq=}} reported that “ugly bombs defile the sacred precincts of Ise” and “the Americans reveal their {{ill|brutal|ja|鬼畜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/brutal|qq=}} nature,” and on {{ill|January 17|ja|1月17日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/January 17|qq=}}, the {{ill|Greater Japan Association for National Salvation|ja|大日本言論報国会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Greater Japan Association for National Salvation|qq=}} held an “All-Nation Outrage Rally” at the {{ill|Hibiya Public Hall|ja|日比谷公会堂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hibiya Public Hall|qq=}} in Tokyo<ref name="mj1"/>.
=== Shrine Defense by the Army and Navy === In response to this air raid, the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army|ja|大日本帝国陸軍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Japanese Army|qq=}} deployed the Ujiyamada Air Defense Unit in February<ref>三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：104ページ</ref>. To defend Ise Grand Shrine, a 672‐man Independent Anti‑Aircraft Battalion No. 5 (an elite unit from Nagoya) and a 1,648‑man Ise Security Force were organized and stationed in Ujiyamada City<ref name="mj2">原（1995）：58ページ</ref>; these units were tasked not only with combating a U.S. landing but also with defending Ise Grand Shrine<ref name=":0" />. The {{ill|anti‑aircraft gun|ja|高射砲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/anti‑aircraft gun|qq=}} positions had been established on land purchased and leveled since the late Taishō period for the royal guesthouse “Ise Rikyu” (a project halted by the war)<ref name=":0" />. Multiple anti‑aircraft positions existed – on a plateau in Nakamura Town, for example, three ammunition bunkers and concrete foundations for anti‑aircraft guns were discovered<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|和書|url=https://miesensoiseki.jimdofree.com/%E6%B6%88%E6%BB%85%E3%81%97%E3%81%9F%E6%88%A6%E4%BA%89%E9%81%BA%E8%B7%A1/|title=Disappeared War Ruins – miesensoiseki Page!|access-date=2023-10-06|publisher=三重県歴史教育者協議会}}</ref>, and a concrete structure—considered an anti‑aircraft ammunition depot and a war ruin—remains on the north side of {{ill|Isuzu Junior High School, Ise City|ja|伊勢市立五十鈴中学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isuzu Junior High School, Ise City|qq=}}<ref>三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：104–105ページ</ref>.
Also that year, during the {{ill|First Mobilization for Defense|ja|第一次兵備|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/First Mobilization for Defense|qq=}}, the {{ill|153rd Division (Japanese Army)|ja|第153師団|lt=153rd Division|lt_ja=第153師団|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/153rd Division (Japanese Army)|qq=}} (also known as the Protecting Tokyo Division) was deployed around Ujiyamada City to defend the entrance to Ise Bay and the shrine<ref name="mj2"/>. The 153rd Division assigned its main infantry regiments to the Shima Peninsula{{#tag:ref|Specifically, the 442nd Infantry Regiment covered the area south of {{ill|Matoya Bay|ja|的矢湾|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matoya Bay|qq=}}, the 443rd from north of Matoya Bay to east of {{ill|Miyagawa (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|lt=Miyagawa|lt_ja=宮川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyagawa (Mie)|qq=}}, and the 444th for the Myonogahara area west of Miyagawa<ref name="mj2"/>.|group="注"}}, while the 441st Infantry Regiment was stationed on the opposite shore in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefecture|qq=}}’s {{ill|Atsumi Peninsula|ja|渥美半島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atsumi Peninsula|qq=}}, with the shrine area defended by the Ise Security Force<ref name="mj2"/>.
The {{ill|Imperial Japanese Navy|ja|大日本帝国海軍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Japanese Navy|qq=}} also installed approximately 194 {{ill|mines|ja|機雷|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/mines|qq=}} off the coasts of {{ill|Sugashima|ja|菅島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugashima|qq=}} and {{ill|Kamijima (Mie)|ja|神島 (三重県)|lt=Kamijima|lt_ja=神島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamijima (Mie)|qq=}} to prevent enemy vessels from entering Ise Bay, and deployed the 4th Kamikaze Squadron to the Shima Peninsula{{#tag:ref|Specifically, the 13th Assault Unit was responsible for the area around {{ill|Toba Town|ja|鳥羽町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toba Town|qq=}}, while the 19th Assault Unit covered the regions around Matoya Bay, {{ill|Eigo Bay|ja|英虞湾|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eigo Bay|qq=}}, and {{ill|Gokasho Bay|ja|五ヶ所湾|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokasho Bay|qq=}}; hangars for the {{ill|Shinyō|ja|震洋|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinyō|qq=}}, {{ill|Kaiten|ja|回天|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaiten|qq=}}, {{ill|Koryū|ja|蛟竜 (潜水艦)|lt=Koryū|lt_ja=蛟竜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koryū|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kairyū|ja|海龍 (潜水艇)|lt=Kairyū|lt_ja=海龍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kairyū|qq=}} were under construction at various sites when the war ended<ref>原（1995）：58–59ページ</ref>.|group="注"}}<ref name="mj2"/>.
Such an extensive defense system for a shrine was unique in Japan and clearly demonstrates how highly valued Ise Grand Shrine was<ref>原（1995）：59ページ</ref>.
=== Recurring Air Raids === On {{ill|January 28|ja|1月28日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/January 28|qq=}}, carrier‐based aircraft conducted machine‑gun attacks<ref name="ih4"/>. On {{ill|February 15|ja|2月15日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/February 15|qq=}}, bombs were dropped on {{ill|Ichinoki Town|ja|一之木町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinoki Town|qq=}}, and in the {{ill|Hamagō Village|ja|浜郷村|lt=Hamagō Region|lt_ja=浜郷地域|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamagō Village|qq=}} and nearby {{ill|Mimori Village|ja|御薗村|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimori Village|qq=}}, {{ill|Electron Incendiary Bombs|ja|エレクトロン焼夷弾|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Electron Incendiary Bombs|qq=}} were dropped<ref name="ss0">日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：240ページ</ref>{{#tag:ref|According to the <nowiki>『伊勢市史』</nowiki>, on {{ill|February 14|ja|2月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/February 14|qq=}}, oil‐filled {{ill|incendiary bombs|ja|焼夷弾|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/incendiary bombs|qq=}} and small bombs were dropped, causing minor {{ill|fires|ja|火災|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fires|qq=}}, but the damage was minimal<ref name="ih4"/>.|group="注"}}. Near {{ill|Yamato Hime Palace|ja|倭姫宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Hime Palace|qq=}}, fires broke out due to incendiary bombs<ref name="tm9">三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：299ページ</ref>, resulting in 1 fatality and 4 minor injuries<ref name="ss0"/>. On {{ill|March 14|ja|3月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/March 14|qq=}}, 20 oil‐filled incendiary bombs and 2 small bombs were dropped on forests in Maeyama Town, but they failed to detonate, causing no damage<ref name="ss0"/>.
On {{ill|April 7|ja|4月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/April 7|qq=}}, bombs were dropped on Ichinoki Town (13 bombs) and on Tate Town (8 bombs)<ref name="ss0"/>, igniting fires in forests and fields and destroying uninhabited houses<ref name="ih4"/>. At the Inner Shrine, 60 glass panes were shattered at guard posts such as the one in front of {{ill|Ujibashi|ja|宇治橋 (伊勢市)|lt=Ujibashi|lt_ja=宇治橋|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ujibashi|qq=}}, where {{ill|Shrine Guards|ja|神宮衛士|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Guards|qq=}} were stationed<ref name="ah1208"/>.
=== P-51 Gunfire === The air raid at 11:20 a.m. on {{ill|April 22|ja|4月22日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/April 22|qq=}} was characterized by gunfire from approximately 40 {{ill|P-51|ja|P-51 (航空機)|lt=P-51|lt_ja=P-51|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/P-51|qq=}} aircraft<ref name="ss0"/>. The P‑51s, divided into several formations, executed a rolling attack that affected not only Ujiyamada City but also nearby areas including {{ill|Futami Town (Mie)|ja|二見町 (三重県)|lt=Futami Town|lt_ja=二見町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futami Town (Mie)|qq=}}, {{ill|Omata Town (Mie)|ja|小俣町 (三重県)|lt=Omata Town|lt_ja=小俣町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omata Town (Mie)|qq=}}, {{ill|Jōda Village (Mie)|ja|城田村 (三重県)|lt=Jōda Village|lt_ja=城田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōda Village (Mie)|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kitahama Village (Mie)|ja|北浜村 (三重県)|lt=Kitahama Village|lt_ja=北浜村|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitahama Village (Mie)|qq=}}<ref name="ss0"/>. At the {{ill|Kobe Steel Electric Yamada Factory|ja|シンフォニア テクノロジー|lt=Kobe Steel Electric|lt_ja=神鋼電機|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobe Steel Electric Yamada Factory|qq=}}, one building was completely burned down; additionally, one house, one unoccupied house, and one vessel were damaged, resulting in 2 deaths and 14 injuries<ref name="ih4"/>. Notably, one P‑51 crashed near the fields of {{ill|Toyohama Village (Mie)|ja|豊浜村 (三重県)|lt=Toyohama Village|lt_ja=豊浜村|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyohama Village (Mie)|qq=}}<ref name="ss0"/>.
=== Air Raids in May and June === [[File:Jingu-Kogakkan University.JPG|thumb|150px|{{ill|Jingu Kōgakkan University|ja|神宮皇學館大学|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingu Kōgakkan University|qq=}} (1941 [Showa 16])]] In the air raid on {{ill|May 14|ja|5月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/May 14|qq=}}, three buildings of {{ill|Jingu Kōgakkan University|ja|皇學館大学|lt=Jingu Kōgakkan University|lt_ja=神宮皇學館大学|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingu Kōgakkan University|qq=}} were partially or completely burned, and one {{ill|national school|ja|国民学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/national school|qq=}} in the city was destroyed<ref name="tm9"/>.
The {{ill|Kobe Steel Electric Yamada Factory|ja|神鋼電機山田工場|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobe Steel Electric Yamada Factory|qq=}} continued to be targeted after April 22 and was hit on both {{ill|June 5|ja|6月5日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June 5|qq=}} and {{ill|June 15|ja|6月15日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June 15|qq=}}<ref name="ss0"/>. In the June 15 air raid, a fire broke out at {{ill|Jinja Port|ja|神社港|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinja Port|qq=}}<ref name="tm0">三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：300ページ</ref>, bombs struck nearby {{ill|Isshiki Town|ja|一色町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isshiki Town|qq=}}, and 14 fatalities were reported<ref name="ss0"/>. Bombs were then dropped consecutively on {{ill|June 16|ja|6月16日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June 16|qq=}} and on {{ill|June 17|ja|6月17日|lt=17th|lt_ja=17日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June 17|qq=}}, followed by several B‑29s dropping bombs on {{ill|June 25|ja|6月25日|lt=25th|lt_ja=25日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June 25|qq=}}<ref name="tm0"/>, and finally on {{ill|June 26|ja|6月26日|lt=26th|lt_ja=26日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June 26|qq=}}, bombs were dropped on {{ill|Funakoe Town|ja|船江 (伊勢市)|lt=Funakoe Town|lt_ja=船江町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Funakoe Town|qq=}} in Ujiyamada City<ref>日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：240–241ページ</ref>.
=== Tense July === In July, the situation became even more critical, with 101 air raid alerts and 24 {{ill|air raid warnings|ja|空襲警報|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/air raid warnings|qq=}} issued<ref name="ss9"/>. On {{ill|July 2|ja|7月2日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 2|qq=}}, the {{ill|police|ja|警察|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/police|qq=}}, represented by the {{ill|Mie Prefectural Police Department|ja|三重県警察部|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Police Department|qq=}}, instructed every shrine in Mie Prefecture to either keep their {{ill|sacred objects|ja|神体|1=Shintai|lt=Goshintai|lt_ja=ご神体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sacred objects|13=User:Immanuelle/Shintai|qq=}} in continuously secure locations unlikely to be affected by spreading fires or desecration, or to relocate them when an air raid warning was issued<ref name="tm7"/>. At Ise Grand Shrine, plans for evacuating the sacred objects had long been in place; the Outer Shrine had an evacuation site near the {{ill|Takakurayama Kofun (Ise)|lt=Takakurayama Kofun (Ise)|lt=Takakurayama Kofun|ja|高倉山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takakurayama Kofun|qq=}}, and the Inner Shrine established one deep within the main sanctuary. However, these specific locations remain classified, known only to a few and left uninvestigated after the war due to their sacred nature<ref name="tm7"/>. It is also unclear whether the sacred objects were ever actually evacuated<ref name="tm7"/>.
On {{ill|July 24|ja|7月24日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 24|qq=}}, bombings ignited a fire in the Outer Shrine’s grounds<ref name="tm1">三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：301ページ</ref>.
=== July 28–29, The Largest Air Raid === [[File:Kiyono Iba Shrine.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kiyono Iba Shrine|ja|清野井庭神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiyono Iba Shrine|qq=}} (2013 [Heisei 25])]] On the night of {{ill|July 27|ja|7月27日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 27|qq=}}, the {{ill|United States Armed Forces|ja|アメリカ軍|lt=US military|lt_ja=アメリカ軍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/United States Armed Forces|qq=}} distributed {{ill|Dentan|ja|伝単|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dentan|qq=}} leaflets warning of an imminent air raid – not only in Ujiyamada City but also in Tsu City, in {{ill|Ichinomiya City, Aichi|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya City, Aichi|qq=}}, in {{ill|Ogaki City, Gifu|ja|大垣市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogaki City, Gifu|qq=}}, in {{ill|Aomori City, Aomori|ja|青森市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aomori City, Aomori|qq=}}, and in {{ill|Uwajima City, Ehime|ja|宇和島市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uwajima City, Ehime|qq=}}<ref name="/furusato-shinbun">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://furusato-shinbun.jp/2013/07/11-79.html|title=B29 Distributed Dentan Leaflets in Tsu to Demoralize—Revealing the Horrors of War; Secret Materials from Mr. Kumoi Unveiled|publisher=三重ふるさと新聞|date=2013-07-11|accessdate=2015-01-25|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150125093845/http://furusato-shinbun.jp/2013/07/11-79.html|archivedate=2015-01-25}}</ref>. At 11:10 p.m. on {{ill|July 28|ja|7月28日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 28|qq=}}, an air raid warning was issued and soon after, about 60 B‑29s arrived from the south of the Shima Peninsula, heading toward Tsu City<ref name="ss1">日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：241ページ</ref>. Then, after midnight on {{ill|July 29|ja|7月29日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 29|qq=}}, around 1:00 a.m., from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|lt=Yamada Station|lt_ja=山田駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Station|qq=}}, approximately 10,000+ 6‑pound ({{ill|pound|ja|ポンド (質量)|lt=pound|lt_ja=ポンド|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/pound|qq=}}) oil incendiary bombs were dropped on the western part of Ujiyamada’s urban area<ref name="ss1"/><ref name="ih5"/>. According to U.S. military records, at that time 93 B‑29s carried out an attack delivering 734.6 {{ill|ton|ja|トン|lt=ton|lt_ja=t|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ton|qq=}} of incendiary bombs<ref name="ss1"/>.
The damage extended over an area of 27,751.35 {{ill|square meters|ja|平方メートル|lt=m<sup>2</sup>|lt_ja=m<sup>2</sup>|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square meters|qq=}} – about 50% of the city’s urban area – with 4,517 households (approximately 30% of all households) completely destroyed and 22,600 people (about 35% of the total population) affected{{#tag:ref|According to the <nowiki>『伊勢市史』</nowiki><ref name="ih5"/>; the “History of the {{ill|Ise Police Station|ja|伊勢警察署|lt=Ise Police Station|lt_ja=宇治山田警察署|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Police Station|qq=}}” reports 4,859 households destroyed, 75 deaths, and 111 injuries.<ref name="ss1"/>|group="注"}}.
Among the damaged facilities were many major ones – including Yamada Station; {{ill|Jingu Kōgakkan University|ja|神宮皇學館大学|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingu Kōgakkan University|qq=}}; the Yamada Branch Office of the {{ill|Ministry of Finance Monopoly Bureau|ja|大蔵省専売局|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Finance Monopoly Bureau|qq=}}; the Doka Regional Office of {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefecture|qq=}}; {{ill|Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Junior High School|ja|三重県立宇治山田高等学校|lt=Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Middle School|lt_ja=三重県立宇治山田中学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Junior High School|qq=}}; {{ill|Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Commercial School|ja|三重県立宇治山田商業高等学校|lt=Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Commercial School|lt_ja=三重県立宇治山田商業学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Commercial School|qq=}}; {{ill|Ise City Welfare Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立厚生小学校|lt=Ujiyamada City Welfare National School|lt_ja=宇治山田市立厚生国民学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Welfare Elementary School|qq=}}; {{ill|Ise City Miyama Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立宮山小学校|lt=Ujiyamada City Miyama National School|lt_ja=宇治山田市立宮山国民学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Miyama Elementary School|qq=}}; and {{ill|Suhara Grand Shrine|ja|須原大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suhara Grand Shrine|qq=}}, among others<ref name="ih5"/>. Notably, Yamada Station, Ujiyamada Junior High, the Welfare National School, and the Doka Regional Office were completely destroyed<ref name="ss1"/>.
Among shrine‐related facilities, the Uji Workshop of the Shrine Administration, the former {{ill|Ministry of Home Affairs|ja|内務省 (日本)|lt=Ministry of Home Affairs|lt_ja=内務省|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Home Affairs|qq=}} Shrine‐related Facilities Construction Office, {{ill|Kiyono Iba Shrine|ja|清野井庭神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiyono Iba Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Ōma Kunio Shrine|ja|大間国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōma Kunio Shrine|qq=}}, and {{ill|Shingu Chōkokan|ja|神宮徴古館|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shingu Chōkokan|qq=}} were damaged<ref name="ih5"/>. It appears that due to prior reconnaissance, the division headquarters located at {{ill|Jingu Kōgakkan|ja|神宮皇學館|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingu Kōgakkan|qq=}} was intensively targeted – and at that time, the adjacent {{ill|Shingu Chōkokan|ja|神宮徴古館|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shingu Chōkokan|qq=}} was completely burned down<ref name=":0"/>.
In the Outer Shrine, incendiary bombs rained even on the inner area of the main enclosure ({{#tag:ref|The inner boundary (みかきうち) refers to the sacred area inside the four {{ill|tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tamagaki|qq=}} that surround the Outer Shrine’s main hall, lying inside the outermost wooden fence.|group="注"}}), yet the inner area was not engulfed in flames<ref name="kg4">矢野（2006）：184ページ</ref>. At {{ill|Tagami Shrine|ja|多賀宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagami Shrine|qq=}}, although the stairs burned, the security force extinguished the fire by smearing themselves on it, and the shrine remained unscathed<ref name="kg4"/>. Later, the remnants of the incendiary bombs removed from the Outer Shrine precinct reportedly amounted to the load of three trucks<ref name="kg4"/>. Moreover, another subsidiary shrine of the Outer Shrine, {{ill|Tsukiyomi Shrine|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi Shrine|qq=}}, in an area where all nearby houses were burned, suffered only superficial impact – its thatched roof merely had bombs embedded in it without detonation, and thanks to strenuous firefighting by the military, only the shrine building was left charred<ref>矢野（2006）：184–185ページ</ref>. However, contracted shrine guards lost their lives in the air raid, and the head priest sustained severe burns<ref name="kg5">矢野（2006）：185ページ</ref>.
Approximately 40 U.S. aircraft formations approached the Inner Shrine as well, but the bombing halted at the mountain on the opposite bank of the {{ill|Isuzu River|ja|五十鈴川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isuzu River|qq=}}, where anti‑aircraft gun positions<ref name=":1"/> or searchlights<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://tetsukujira.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-1295.html |title=Ise Diary in Wartime – FC2 Version|access-date=2023-10-06|publisher=てっつん}}</ref> were deployed, sparing the Inner Shrine from damage<ref name="kg4"/>. The fact that the Inner Shrine was unharmed was hailed by the priests as a “miracle,” and they wept in gratitude for Ise Grand Shrine’s divine protection<ref name="kg4"/>. Although the guard house of {{ill|Yamato Hime Palace|ja|倭姫宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Hime Palace|qq=}} – a building responsible for transmitting offerings for {{ill|Kagura|ja|神楽|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagura|qq=}} and {{ill|Sacred Meal|ja|神饌|lt=Sacred Food|lt_ja=御饌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sacred Meal|qq=}}, as well as for conferring {{ill|Divine Hemp|ja|神宮大麻|lt=Divine Hemp|lt_ja=大麻|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Hemp|qq=}} and protective charms ({{ill|Omamori|ja|お守り|lt=Omamori|lt_ja=守祓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omamori|qq=}}) – was destroyed, the main shrine building remained intact<ref name="kg5"/>. Regarding this, military historian {{ill|Hara Takeshi|ja|原剛 (軍事史家)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hara Takeshi|qq=}} of the {{ill|Defense Ministry|ja|防衛省|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Defense Ministry|qq=}} and the {{ill|Defense Research Institute|ja|防衛研究所|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Defense Research Institute|qq=}} explained that by then the U.S. had imposed bombing restrictions on Japanese cultural facilities, with Ise Grand Shrine being specifically mentioned in their guidelines<ref name="mj2"/>.
=== August Air Raids and the End of the War === Even after the massive air raid on {{ill|July 29|ja|7月29日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 29|qq=}}, on the night of {{ill|August 1|ja|8月1日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 1|qq=}}, about 25 B‑29s attacked, and on {{ill|August 14|ja|8月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 14|qq=}}, small bombs and {{ill|machine gun fire|ja|機銃掃射|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/machine gun fire|qq=}} were directed at Miyagoto Town and in front of Yamada Station<ref>日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：205, 241ページ</ref>. Then, on {{ill|August 15|ja|8月15日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 15|qq=}} at noon, the {{ill|Jewel Voice Broadcast|ja|玉音放送|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jewel Voice Broadcast|qq=}} was heard, marking Japan’s {{ill|end of the war|ja|終戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/end of the war|qq=}}<ref>三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：302ページ</ref>. It is said that at Ise Grand Shrine, executives gathered in the main office of the Shrine Administration and, with tears and sobs, listened to the broadcast<ref name="kg1">矢野（2006）：181ページ</ref>. Meanwhile, cannons and other war trophies from the {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|ja|日露戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Russo-Japanese War|qq=}} that were on display in the shrine grounds were burned overnight by the military using burners and then buried<ref>矢野（2006）：181–182ページ</ref>.
== Post-Air Raid Conditions == [[File:Ise Shrine Geku Sengyo-no-gi 1953.jpg|thumb|250x250px|The first post-war Sengu (Shrine Relocation Ceremony) held in {{ill|1953|ja|1953|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1953|qq=}} (Showa 28)]] [[File:Ise Shrine Geku area Aerial photograph.1983.jpg|thumb|270px|The rebuilt Ise City urban area and Outer Shrine (1983 [Showa 58])<br/><small>{{国土航空写真}}</small>]] After the war, Ise Grand Shrine disassociated itself from {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/State Shinto|qq=}} and became a {{ill|religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/religious corporation|qq=}}<ref name="sj"/><ref>伊勢文化舎 編（2009）：13ページ</ref>. The Allied forces frequently crossed {{ill|jeep|ja|ジープ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/jeep|qq=}} over Ujibashi, attempting to enter the sacred precincts and troubling the shrine guards<ref>矢野（2006）：188ページ</ref>. Moreover, when an inspection was made by the {{ill|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|ja|連合国軍最高司令官総司令部|lt=GHQ|lt_ja=GHQ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|qq=}}, there was a threat that the shrine’s area might be reduced; however, the then-superintendent cleverly argued, “The sacred precincts visible from Ujibashi are essential for nature conservation,” and this was accepted, thus preserving the shrine’s grounds<ref>矢野（2006）：189ページ</ref>. Pilgrimage numbers plummeted – by {{ill|1947|ja|1947|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1947|qq=}} (Showa 22), the number of Outer Shrine pilgrims had dropped to one-tenth of the {{ill|1940|ja|1940|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1940|qq=}} (Showa 15) figures<ref name="sj"/>. This decline has been attributed to social chaos<ref name="nm"/>, as a reaction against pre-war forced pilgrimages<ref name="sj"/>, and also to rumors that military police were detaining pilgrims at Ujibashi and deporting them to {{ill|Okinawa under U.S. administration|ja|アメリカ合衆国による沖縄統治|lt=Okinawa|lt_ja=沖縄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okinawa under U.S. administration|qq=}}<ref name="kg2">矢野（2006）：182ページ</ref>. The Sengu originally scheduled for {{ill|1949|ja|1949|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1949|qq=}} (Showa 24) was postponed in deference to public sentiment and the wishes of {{ill|Emperor Showa|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Showa|qq=}}, and with mounting calls to rebuild Ujibashi, reconstruction was undertaken in 1949 (Showa 24), with the postponed 59th Sengu subsequently held four years later in {{ill|1953|ja|1953|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1953|qq=}} (Showa 28)<ref>伊勢文化舎 編（2009）：13–14ページ</ref>. Thereafter, it became customary to rebuild Ujibashi four years before each Sengu ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengyo|qq=}})<ref>伊勢文化舎 編（2009）：14ページ</ref>.
== Air Raid Exhibition Held == In March {{ill|1972|ja|1972|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1972|qq=}} (Showa 47), officials from {{ill|Chiku Rō|ja|地区労|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiku Rō|qq=}} advocated for recording the Ujiyamada Air Raid and submitted a petition titled “Issuance of a Publication Document Recording the Air Raids in Ise City and the Establishment of a Peace Memorial Day.” This petition was adopted by the Ise City Council in January {{ill|1975|ja|1975|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1975|qq=}} (Showa 50)<ref name="jcr">{{Cite web|和書|author=三重県本部伊勢市職|title=戦後五〇年の取り組み|url=https://www.jichiro.gr.jp/jichiken_kako/report/jichikensyo/pdf/3rd_katsudou.pdf|date=1996|accessdate=2015-01-24|archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2015-0124-2116-48/https://www.jichiro.gr.jp:443/jichiken_kako/report/jichikensyo/pdf/3rd_katsudou.pdf|archivedate=2015-01-24}}</ref>. The central figure in this petition, {{ill|Yamakawa Tadazō|ja|山川忠三|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamakawa Tadazō|qq=}}, went on to form the “Association for Recording the Ise City Air Raid,” organizing air raid exhibitions and publishing newsletters detailing the events and personal testimonies<ref name="jcr"/>. Subsequently, the exhibition was held in an organizing committee format, with both Ise City and the Ise City Board of Education as co‑sponsors<ref name="jcr"/>. In {{ill|1988|ja|1988|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1988|qq=}} (Showa 63), the history club of {{ill|Mie Prefectural Ise High School|ja|三重県立伊勢高等学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Ise High School|qq=}} created an incendiary bomb map of Ujiyamada City based on archival materials and interviews, which then became the exhibition’s central display<ref name="jcr"/>. In {{ill|1995|ja|1995|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1995|qq=}} (Heisei 7), marking 50 years since the war, Ise Youth Theater (now known as Gekidan Ise) staged the play “Ise Great Air Raid” on the anniversary of the July 29 air raid<ref name="jcr"/>.

revision.text:
[[File:Bombing of Ujiyamada at Ozeko-cho.jpg|thumb|After the Ujiyamada Air Raid, Ōzeko‐chō in Ujiyamada City – {{ill|Ise Ginza Shindō Shopping District|ja|伊勢銀座新道商店街|lt=New Road|lt_ja=新道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Ginza Shindō Shopping District|qq=}} area]] [[File:Bombing of Ujiyamada Map, Shima Peninsula.png|thumb|300px|Map related to the Ujiyamada Air Raid (Wide area of the Shima Peninsula)]] [[File:Bombing of Ujiyamada Map, Central City.png|thumb|300px|Map related to the Ujiyamada Air Raid (Ujiyamada City urban area)]]
'''Ujiyamada Air Raid''' (宇治山田空襲) was an [[:en:Airstrike|air raid]] ([[:en:Strategic bombing|strategic bombing]]) conducted by the {{ill|United States Armed Forces|ja|アメリカ合衆国軍|lt=US military|lt_ja=アメリカ軍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/United States Armed Forces|qq=}} at the end of [[:en:World War II|World War II]] in {{ill|1945|ja|1945|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1945|qq=}} (Showa 20) on Ujiyamada City in [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]] (present-day [[:en:Ise, Mie|Ise City]]). Both the Japanese authorities and the Shima Peninsula had stationed troops in anticipation that it would serve as one of the landing sites for the {{ill|United States Armed Forces|ja|アメリカ合衆国軍|lt=US military|lt_ja=アメリカ軍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/United States Armed Forces|qq=}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.asahi.com/area/mie/articles/MTW20120820251060001.html |title=朝日新聞デジタル：【６】高射砲 Ｂ２９に届かず - 三重 - 地域|access-date=2023-10-06|publisher=朝日新聞社}}</ref><ref name="mj2" />. However, contemporary Japanese press condemned the American side on the premise that the bombing was intended to dampen the fighting spirit of the Japanese people by attacking Ujiyamada, a city of national importance often referred to as the “Divine Capital.”<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tomioka-aichi.jp/isan/sensoutaiken/pdf-taiken/16-tokumei.pdf|title=16|author=[[:en:Anonymity|Anonymous]]|publisher=ふるさと遺産を保存する会（富岡ふるさと会館）|accessdate=2014-11-29|archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2014-1129-1509-46/tomioka-aichi.jp/isan/sensoutaiken/pdf-taiken/16-tokumei.pdf|archivedate=2014-11-29}}</ref>
[[:en:January 14|January 14]]’s [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]{{#tag:ref|伊勢神宮は正式名称を「神宮」と称し、皇大神宮（内宮）と豊受大神宮（外宮）の2つの正宮に別宮・摂社・末社・所管社と呼ばれる宮社が付属し、合計125社から構成される<ref>三橋（2013）：19 - 20ページ</ref><ref>JTBパブリッシング（2011）：24ページ</ref>。本文中で取り上げる神社は、須原大社を除いて伊勢神宮を構成する125社に含まれる。詳細は「[[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]」および「{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|lt=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|lt=List of the 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of the 125 Shrines of Ise|qq=}}」を参照。|group="注"}}{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|lt=Outer Shrine|lt_ja=外宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Daijingu|qq=}} was the target of the initial bombing, and thereafter the shrine suffered six large‐scale attacks that burned 50–60% of the urban area{{#tag:ref|『伊勢市史』<ref name="ih5">伊勢市 編（1968）：445ページ</ref>および『日本地誌 第13巻』の記述<ref name="nm">日本地誌研究所 編（1976）：353ページ</ref>。[[三重県庁]]ウェブサイト内では「市内の約60%を焼失」と記している<ref name="bm"/>。|group="注"}}.
== Overview == The {{ill|Shima Peninsula|ja|志摩半島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima Peninsula|qq=}} was an attractive target for the B‑29 – along with [[:en:Cape Shionomisaki|Cape Shio]] and {{ill|Omaezaki|ja|御前崎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omaezaki|qq=}} – so the B‑29 frequently traversed the skies above Ujiyamada City, which lies at the base of the Shima Peninsula<ref name="ss2">日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：202ページ</ref>. Ujiyamada City’s proximity to the open sea also made it vulnerable to attacks by [[:en:Navalised aircraft|naval aircraft]] in an urban setting<ref name="ss2"/>. According to records by Kishihara Monjirō of Miyagoto Town, from {{ill|1944|ja|1944|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1944|qq=}} (Showa 19) through [[:en:August 16|August 16]], 501 air raid alerts and 99 air raid warnings were issued<ref name="ss9"/>.
Air raid casualties numbered 101 dead and 240 injured, with 4,928 households partially or completely burned and 22 households destroyed<ref name="ym5">稲本ほか（2000）：285ページ</ref>. According to Inamoto Kisho et al. in <nowiki>『三重県の歴史』</nowiki>, although the scale of damage was smaller than that in other Mie cities such as [[:en:Tsu, Mie|Tsu City]], [[:en:Yokkaichi|Yokkaichi]], and [[:en:Kuwana, Mie|Kuwana City]], the number of days on which air raids occurred was greater<ref name="ym5"/>.
== Conditions Prior to the Air Raid == After the [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]], the government promoted the {{ill|Shinto State Religion|ja|神道国教化|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto State Religion|qq=}}, and the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] was positioned as the highest‐Ranking [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrine]] in Japan<ref>新田（2014）：38ページ</ref>. With the development of modern {{ill|transportation|ja|交通機関|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/transportation|qq=}} and the linking of Ise Grand Shrine with [[:en:Statism|nationalism]], the number of pilgrims increased continuously from {{ill|1897|ja|1897|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1897|qq=}} (Meiji 30) through {{ill|1945|ja|1945|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1945|qq=}} (Showa 20)<ref name="sj">新田（2014）：39ページ</ref>. Ujiyamada City, known as the “Divine Capital”, became a magnet for people and wealth from across Japan<ref name="tm7">三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：107ページ</ref>.
In February {{ill|1933|ja|1933|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1933|qq=}} (Showa 8), the Ujiyamada City Mayor submitted an “Opinion Document Concerning the State‐Managed Special Urban Planning for the Divine Capital” addressed to the {{ill|Prime Minister|ja|Prime Minister of Japan|1=Prime Minister of Japan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prime Minister|13=User:Immanuelle/Prime Minister of Japan|qq=}} and the [[:en:Interior minister|Minister of Home Affairs]], proposing that the old downtown be redeveloped into parkland, roads, and hotel sites befitting the Divine Capital, that a new downtown be constructed in the suburbs for displaced citizens, and that a [[:en:Rapid transit|subway]] and an [[:en:Airport|airport]] be built<ref name="tm8">三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：108ページ</ref>. In response, in {{ill|1940|ja|1940|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1940|qq=}} (Showa 15) – the year marking the {{ill|Kigenshiki 2600|ja|紀元二千六百年記念行事|lt=Emperor’s 2600th Anniversary|lt_ja=皇紀2600|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigenshiki 2600|qq=}} – the “Special Urban Planning Act for Shrine‐related Areas” was enacted<ref name="tm8"/>. Under this law, however, no new downtown was planned; only the expansion of Ise Grand Shrine’s precincts and the improvement of railways and roads were carried out<ref name="tm8"/>.
Even after the outbreak of the [[:en:Pacific War|Pacific War]], Ise Grand Shrine remained relatively calm until around the beginning of {{ill|1943|ja|1943|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1943|qq=}} (Showa 18)<ref name="kg3">矢野（2006）：183ページ</ref>. However, from April of that year, the [[:en:Nightlight|permanent lantern]] was extinguished and air raid alerts and warnings became frequent, with pilgrims increasingly engaging in victory prayers organized by the [[:en:Military|military]] and local associations ([[:en:Chōnaikai|chōnaikai]])<ref name="kg3"/>. Amid these tense conditions, preparations for the scheduled {{ill|Sengu|ja|神宮式年遷宮|lt=Shrine Relocation Ceremony|lt_ja=式年遷宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengu|qq=}} in {{ill|1949|ja|1949|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1949|qq=}} (Showa 24) continued steadily<ref name="kg3"/>.
== Chronology of the Air Raid == === Damage to the Outer Shrine in the First Air Raid === [[File:Kaguraden Hall of Toyouke Grand Shrine.jpg|thumb|Outer Shrine Kaguraden (2019 [Heisei 31])]] On [[:en:January 14|January 14]] {{ill|1945|ja|1945|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1945|qq=}} (Showa 20) at 2:53 p.m., a B‑29 of the [[:en:United States Armed Forces|US military]] attacked Ujiyamada City<ref name="ss9">日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：239ページ</ref>{{#tag:ref|Of the 62 B‑29s that bombed the {{ill|Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Nagoya Aircraft Manufacturing Works|ja|三菱重工業名古屋航空宇宙システム製作所|lt=Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Nagoya Aircraft Works|lt_ja=三菱重工業名古屋航空機製作所|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Nagoya Aircraft Manufacturing Works|qq=}}, 3 aircraft on their return flight attacked Ujiyamada City<ref name="mj1">原（1995）：57ページ</ref>.|group="注"}} – marking the first air raid on the city<ref name="ih4">伊勢市 編（1968）：444ページ</ref>. This was the first full‐scale air raid in Mie Prefecture{{#tag:ref|According to the description on the Mie Prefecture government website<ref name="bm"/>. The first air raid in Mie occurred on [[:en:April 18|April 18]] {{ill|1942|ja|1942|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1942|qq=}} (Showa 17) – the [[:en:Doolittle Raid|Doolittle Raid]] – during which [[:en:Yokkaichi|Yokkaichi]] and the area of [[:en:Kuwana District, Mie|Kuwana District]]’s [[:en:Nagashima, Kagoshima|Nagashima Village]] (present-day [[:en:Kuwana, Mie|Kuwana City]]) were strafed by machine guns.<ref name="group="注""/></nowiki>. In this air raid, 1 person was killed and 16 injured{{#tag:ref|According to the <nowiki>『伊勢市史』</nowiki> (see <ref name="ih4"/>) and the “History of the {{ill|Ise Police Station|ja|伊勢警察署|lt=Ise Police Station|lt_ja=宇治山田警察署|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Police Station|qq=}}”, which reports 3 severe and 14 minor injuries.|group="注"}}.
An estimated 8 bombs were dropped<ref name="ih4"/>, striking locations such as the Rensuiyama Orchard in {{ill|Tokiwacho|ja|常磐町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokiwacho|qq=}} and the northwestern end of the Nishikizuwashi Bridge in {{ill|Iwabuchi Town|ja|岩渕町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwabuchi Town|qq=}}<ref name="ss9"/>. On the Outer Shrine, 6 bombs were dropped at 5 spots, damaging the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojōden|qq=}}, {{ill|Kujōden|ja|九丈殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujōden|qq=}}, [[:en:Kagura-den|Kaguraden]], and {{ill|Saikan|ja|斎館|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saikan|qq=}}<nowiki>{{#tag:ref|Gojōden and Kujōden are used for purification rituals during rain and for remote worship at subsidiary and branch shrines, Kaguraden is where invocations are held<ref>JTBパブリッシング（2011）：33, 41ページ</ref>, and Saikan is the residence for Shinto priests<ref>矢野（2006）：47ページ</ref>.|group="注"}}</nowiki>.<ref name="yk">西垣・松島（1974）：247ページ</ref>. The damage was relatively minor – limited to broken eaves, damaged shoji screens, collapsed wooden fences, and a few holes in the roofs<ref name="ah1208">{{Cite web|和書|author=中村尚徳|url=http://www.asahi.com/area/mie/articles/MTW20120818251060001.html|title=[5] Exaggerated Announcement to Boost Morale|work={{ill|Asahi Shimbun Digital|ja|朝日新聞デジタル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asahi Shimbun Digital|qq=}}|publisher=[[:en:The Asahi Shimbun|Asahi Shimbun]]|date=2012-08-18|accessdate=2015-01-25|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150125095304/http://www.asahi.com/area/mie/articles/MTW20120818251060001.html|archivedate=2015-01-25}}</ref>. The shrine interpreted this as a “divine phenomenon”<ref name="kg3"/>. However, 4½ hours later on [[:en:Radio|radio]], the {{ill|Imperial Headquarters Announcement|ja|大本営発表|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Headquarters Announcement|qq=}} reported that “the enemy dropped several bombs in the Toyouke Grand Shrine area, causing two Saikan and five Kaguraden structures to collapse”<ref name="yk"/>. In response, the [[:en:Newspaper|newspaper]] on [[:en:January 15|January 15]] reported that “ugly bombs defile the sacred precincts of Ise” and “the Americans reveal their {{ill|brutal|ja|鬼畜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/brutal|qq=}} nature,” and on [[:en:January 17|January 17]], the {{ill|Greater Japan Association for National Salvation|ja|大日本言論報国会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Greater Japan Association for National Salvation|qq=}} held an “All-Nation Outrage Rally” at the {{ill|Hibiya Public Hall|ja|日比谷公会堂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hibiya Public Hall|qq=}} in Tokyo<ref name="mj1"/>.
=== Shrine Defense by the Army and Navy === In response to this air raid, the [[:en:Imperial Japanese Army|Imperial Japanese Army]] deployed the Ujiyamada Air Defense Unit in February<ref>三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：104ページ</ref>. To defend Ise Grand Shrine, a 672‐man Independent Anti‑Aircraft Battalion No. 5 (an elite unit from Nagoya) and a 1,648‑man Ise Security Force were organized and stationed in Ujiyamada City<ref name="mj2">原（1995）：58ページ</ref>; these units were tasked not only with combating a U.S. landing but also with defending Ise Grand Shrine<ref name=":0" />. The {{ill|anti‑aircraft gun|ja|高射砲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/anti‑aircraft gun|qq=}} positions had been established on land purchased and leveled since the late Taishō period for the royal guesthouse “Ise Rikyu” (a project halted by the war)<ref name=":0" />. Multiple anti‑aircraft positions existed – on a plateau in Nakamura Town, for example, three ammunition bunkers and concrete foundations for anti‑aircraft guns were discovered<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|和書|url=https://miesensoiseki.jimdofree.com/%E6%B6%88%E6%BB%85%E3%81%97%E3%81%9F%E6%88%A6%E4%BA%89%E9%81%BA%E8%B7%A1/|title=Disappeared War Ruins – miesensoiseki Page!|access-date=2023-10-06|publisher=三重県歴史教育者協議会}}</ref>, and a concrete structure—considered an anti‑aircraft ammunition depot and a war ruin—remains on the north side of {{ill|Isuzu Junior High School, Ise City|ja|伊勢市立五十鈴中学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isuzu Junior High School, Ise City|qq=}}<ref>三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：104–105ページ</ref>.
Also that year, during the {{ill|First Mobilization for Defense|ja|第一次兵備|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/First Mobilization for Defense|qq=}}, the {{ill|153rd Division (Japanese Army)|ja|第153師団|lt=153rd Division|lt_ja=第153師団|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/153rd Division (Japanese Army)|qq=}} (also known as the Protecting Tokyo Division) was deployed around Ujiyamada City to defend the entrance to Ise Bay and the shrine<ref name="mj2"/>. The 153rd Division assigned its main infantry regiments to the Shima Peninsula{{#tag:ref|Specifically, the 442nd Infantry Regiment covered the area south of [[:en:Matoya Bay|Matoya Bay]], the 443rd from north of Matoya Bay to east of [[:en:Miya River (Mie)|Miyagawa]], and the 444th for the Myonogahara area west of Miyagawa<ref name="mj2"/>.|group="注"}}, while the 441st Infantry Regiment was stationed on the opposite shore in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]’s [[:en:Atsumi Peninsula|Atsumi Peninsula]], with the shrine area defended by the Ise Security Force<ref name="mj2"/>.
The [[:en:Imperial Japanese Navy|Imperial Japanese Navy]] also installed approximately 194 [[:en:Naval mine|mines]] off the coasts of [[:en:Sugashima|Sugashima]] and [[:en:Kami-shima|Kamijima]] to prevent enemy vessels from entering Ise Bay, and deployed the 4th Kamikaze Squadron to the Shima Peninsula{{#tag:ref|Specifically, the 13th Assault Unit was responsible for the area around {{ill|Toba Town|ja|鳥羽町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toba Town|qq=}}, while the 19th Assault Unit covered the regions around Matoya Bay, [[:en:Ago Bay|Eigo Bay]], and {{ill|Gokasho Bay|ja|五ヶ所湾|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokasho Bay|qq=}}; hangars for the [[:en:Shinyo (suicide motorboat)|Shinyō]], [[:en:Kaiten|Kaiten]], {{ill|Koryū|ja|蛟竜 (潜水艦)|lt=Koryū|lt_ja=蛟竜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koryū|qq=}}, and [[:en:Kairyū-class submarine|Kairyū]] were under construction at various sites when the war ended<ref>原（1995）：58–59ページ</ref>.|group="注"}}<ref name="mj2"/>.
Such an extensive defense system for a shrine was unique in Japan and clearly demonstrates how highly valued Ise Grand Shrine was<ref>原（1995）：59ページ</ref>.
=== Recurring Air Raids === On [[:en:January 28|January 28]], carrier‐based aircraft conducted machine‑gun attacks<ref name="ih4"/>. On [[:en:February 15|February 15]], bombs were dropped on {{ill|Ichinoki Town|ja|一之木町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinoki Town|qq=}}, and in the {{ill|Hamagō Village|ja|浜郷村|lt=Hamagō Region|lt_ja=浜郷地域|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamagō Village|qq=}} and nearby [[:en:Misono, Mie|Mimori Village]], {{ill|Electron Incendiary Bombs|ja|エレクトロン焼夷弾|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Electron Incendiary Bombs|qq=}} were dropped<ref name="ss0">日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：240ページ</ref>{{#tag:ref|According to the <nowiki>『伊勢市史』</nowiki>, on [[:en:February 14|February 14]], oil‐filled [[:en:Incendiary device|incendiary bombs]] and small bombs were dropped, causing minor [[:en:Conflagration|fires]], but the damage was minimal<ref name="ih4"/>.|group="注"}}. Near {{ill|Yamato Hime Palace|ja|倭姫宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Hime Palace|qq=}}, fires broke out due to incendiary bombs<ref name="tm9">三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：299ページ</ref>, resulting in 1 fatality and 4 minor injuries<ref name="ss0"/>. On [[:en:March 14|March 14]], 20 oil‐filled incendiary bombs and 2 small bombs were dropped on forests in Maeyama Town, but they failed to detonate, causing no damage<ref name="ss0"/>.
On [[:en:April 7|April 7]], bombs were dropped on Ichinoki Town (13 bombs) and on Tate Town (8 bombs)<ref name="ss0"/>, igniting fires in forests and fields and destroying uninhabited houses<ref name="ih4"/>. At the Inner Shrine, 60 glass panes were shattered at guard posts such as the one in front of {{ill|Ujibashi|ja|宇治橋 (伊勢市)|lt=Ujibashi|lt_ja=宇治橋|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ujibashi|qq=}}, where {{ill|Shrine Guards|ja|神宮衛士|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Guards|qq=}} were stationed<ref name="ah1208"/>.
=== P-51 Gunfire === The air raid at 11:20 a.m. on [[:en:April 22|April 22]] was characterized by gunfire from approximately 40 [[:en:North American P-51 Mustang|P-51]] aircraft<ref name="ss0"/>. The P‑51s, divided into several formations, executed a rolling attack that affected not only Ujiyamada City but also nearby areas including [[:en:Futami, Mie|Futami Town]], [[:en:Obata, Mie|Omata Town]], {{ill|Jōda Village (Mie)|ja|城田村 (三重県)|lt=Jōda Village|lt_ja=城田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōda Village (Mie)|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kitahama Village (Mie)|ja|北浜村 (三重県)|lt=Kitahama Village|lt_ja=北浜村|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitahama Village (Mie)|qq=}}<ref name="ss0"/>. At the {{ill|Kobe Steel Electric Yamada Factory|ja|シンフォニア テクノロジー|lt=Kobe Steel Electric|lt_ja=神鋼電機|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobe Steel Electric Yamada Factory|qq=}}, one building was completely burned down; additionally, one house, one unoccupied house, and one vessel were damaged, resulting in 2 deaths and 14 injuries<ref name="ih4"/>. Notably, one P‑51 crashed near the fields of {{ill|Toyohama Village (Mie)|ja|豊浜村 (三重県)|lt=Toyohama Village|lt_ja=豊浜村|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyohama Village (Mie)|qq=}}<ref name="ss0"/>.
=== Air Raids in May and June === [[File:Jingu-Kogakkan University.JPG|thumb|150px|{{ill|Jingu Kōgakkan University|ja|神宮皇學館大学|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingu Kōgakkan University|qq=}} (1941 [Showa 16])]] In the air raid on [[:en:May 14|May 14]], three buildings of [[:en:Kogakkan University|Jingu Kōgakkan University]] were partially or completely burned, and one {{ill|national school|ja|国民学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/national school|qq=}} in the city was destroyed<ref name="tm9"/>.
The {{ill|Kobe Steel Electric Yamada Factory|ja|神鋼電機山田工場|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobe Steel Electric Yamada Factory|qq=}} continued to be targeted after April 22 and was hit on both [[:en:June 5|June 5]] and [[:en:June 15|June 15]]<ref name="ss0"/>. In the June 15 air raid, a fire broke out at {{ill|Jinja Port|ja|神社港|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinja Port|qq=}}<ref name="tm0">三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：300ページ</ref>, bombs struck nearby [[:en:Isshiki, Aichi|Isshiki Town]], and 14 fatalities were reported<ref name="ss0"/>. Bombs were then dropped consecutively on [[:en:June 16|June 16]] and on [[:en:June 17|17th]], followed by several B‑29s dropping bombs on [[:en:June 25|25th]]<ref name="tm0"/>, and finally on [[:en:June 26|26th]], bombs were dropped on {{ill|Funakoe Town|ja|船江 (伊勢市)|lt=Funakoe Town|lt_ja=船江町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Funakoe Town|qq=}} in Ujiyamada City<ref>日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：240–241ページ</ref>.
=== Tense July === In July, the situation became even more critical, with 101 air raid alerts and 24 [[:en:Civil defense siren|air raid warnings]] issued<ref name="ss9"/>. On [[:en:July 2|July 2]], the [[:en:Police|police]], represented by the {{ill|Mie Prefectural Police Department|ja|三重県警察部|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Police Department|qq=}}, instructed every shrine in Mie Prefecture to either keep their [[:en:Shintai|Goshintai]] in continuously secure locations unlikely to be affected by spreading fires or desecration, or to relocate them when an air raid warning was issued<ref name="tm7"/>. At Ise Grand Shrine, plans for evacuating the sacred objects had long been in place; the Outer Shrine had an evacuation site near the {{ill|Takakurayama Kofun (Ise)|lt=Takakurayama Kofun (Ise)|lt=Takakurayama Kofun|ja|高倉山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takakurayama Kofun|qq=}}, and the Inner Shrine established one deep within the main sanctuary. However, these specific locations remain classified, known only to a few and left uninvestigated after the war due to their sacred nature<ref name="tm7"/>. It is also unclear whether the sacred objects were ever actually evacuated<ref name="tm7"/>.
On [[:en:July 24|July 24]], bombings ignited a fire in the Outer Shrine’s grounds<ref name="tm1">三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：301ページ</ref>.
=== July 28–29, The Largest Air Raid === [[File:Kiyono Iba Shrine.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kiyono Iba Shrine|ja|清野井庭神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiyono Iba Shrine|qq=}} (2013 [Heisei 25])]] On the night of [[:en:July 27|July 27]], the [[:en:United States Armed Forces|US military]] distributed [[:en:Airborne leaflet propaganda|Dentan]] leaflets warning of an imminent air raid – not only in Ujiyamada City but also in Tsu City, in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya City, Aichi]], in [[:en:Ōgaki|Ogaki City, Gifu]], in [[:en:Aomori|Aomori City, Aomori]], and in [[:en:Uwajima, Ehime|Uwajima City, Ehime]]<ref name="/furusato-shinbun">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://furusato-shinbun.jp/2013/07/11-79.html|title=B29 Distributed Dentan Leaflets in Tsu to Demoralize—Revealing the Horrors of War; Secret Materials from Mr. Kumoi Unveiled|publisher=三重ふるさと新聞|date=2013-07-11|accessdate=2015-01-25|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150125093845/http://furusato-shinbun.jp/2013/07/11-79.html|archivedate=2015-01-25}}</ref>. At 11:10 p.m. on [[:en:July 28|July 28]], an air raid warning was issued and soon after, about 60 B‑29s arrived from the south of the Shima Peninsula, heading toward Tsu City<ref name="ss1">日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：241ページ</ref>. Then, after midnight on [[:en:July 29|July 29]], around 1:00 a.m., from [[:en:Iseshi Station|Yamada Station]], approximately 10,000+ 6‑pound ([[:en:Pound (mass)|pound]]) oil incendiary bombs were dropped on the western part of Ujiyamada’s urban area<ref name="ss1"/><ref name="ih5"/>. According to U.S. military records, at that time 93 B‑29s carried out an attack delivering 734.6 [[:en:Tonne|ton]] of incendiary bombs<ref name="ss1"/>.
The damage extended over an area of 27,751.35 [[:en:Square metre|m<sup>2</sup>]] – about 50% of the city’s urban area – with 4,517 households (approximately 30% of all households) completely destroyed and 22,600 people (about 35% of the total population) affected{{#tag:ref|According to the <nowiki>『伊勢市史』</nowiki><ref name="ih5"/>; the “History of the {{ill|Ise Police Station|ja|伊勢警察署|lt=Ise Police Station|lt_ja=宇治山田警察署|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Police Station|qq=}}” reports 4,859 households destroyed, 75 deaths, and 111 injuries.<ref name="ss1"/>|group="注"}}.
Among the damaged facilities were many major ones – including Yamada Station; {{ill|Jingu Kōgakkan University|ja|神宮皇學館大学|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingu Kōgakkan University|qq=}}; the Yamada Branch Office of the {{ill|Ministry of Finance Monopoly Bureau|ja|大蔵省専売局|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Finance Monopoly Bureau|qq=}}; the Doka Regional Office of {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefecture|qq=}}; {{ill|Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Junior High School|ja|三重県立宇治山田高等学校|lt=Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Middle School|lt_ja=三重県立宇治山田中学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Junior High School|qq=}}; {{ill|Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Commercial School|ja|三重県立宇治山田商業高等学校|lt=Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Commercial School|lt_ja=三重県立宇治山田商業学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Ujiyamada Commercial School|qq=}}; {{ill|Ise City Welfare Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立厚生小学校|lt=Ujiyamada City Welfare National School|lt_ja=宇治山田市立厚生国民学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Welfare Elementary School|qq=}}; {{ill|Ise City Miyama Elementary School|ja|伊勢市立宮山小学校|lt=Ujiyamada City Miyama National School|lt_ja=宇治山田市立宮山国民学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Miyama Elementary School|qq=}}; and {{ill|Suhara Grand Shrine|ja|須原大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suhara Grand Shrine|qq=}}, among others<ref name="ih5"/>. Notably, Yamada Station, Ujiyamada Junior High, the Welfare National School, and the Doka Regional Office were completely destroyed<ref name="ss1"/>.
Among shrine‐related facilities, the Uji Workshop of the Shrine Administration, the former [[:en:Home Ministry|Ministry of Home Affairs]] Shrine‐related Facilities Construction Office, {{ill|Kiyono Iba Shrine|ja|清野井庭神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiyono Iba Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Ōma Kunio Shrine|ja|大間国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōma Kunio Shrine|qq=}}, and {{ill|Shingu Chōkokan|ja|神宮徴古館|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shingu Chōkokan|qq=}} were damaged<ref name="ih5"/>. It appears that due to prior reconnaissance, the division headquarters located at {{ill|Jingu Kōgakkan|ja|神宮皇學館|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingu Kōgakkan|qq=}} was intensively targeted – and at that time, the adjacent {{ill|Shingu Chōkokan|ja|神宮徴古館|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shingu Chōkokan|qq=}} was completely burned down<ref name=":0"/>.
In the Outer Shrine, incendiary bombs rained even on the inner area of the main enclosure ({{#tag:ref|The inner boundary (みかきうち) refers to the sacred area inside the four [[:en:Tamagaki|tamagaki]] that surround the Outer Shrine’s main hall, lying inside the outermost wooden fence.|group="注"}}), yet the inner area was not engulfed in flames<ref name="kg4">矢野（2006）：184ページ</ref>. At {{ill|Tagami Shrine|ja|多賀宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagami Shrine|qq=}}, although the stairs burned, the security force extinguished the fire by smearing themselves on it, and the shrine remained unscathed<ref name="kg4"/>. Later, the remnants of the incendiary bombs removed from the Outer Shrine precinct reportedly amounted to the load of three trucks<ref name="kg4"/>. Moreover, another subsidiary shrine of the Outer Shrine, {{ill|Tsukiyomi Shrine|ja|月夜見宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi Shrine|qq=}}, in an area where all nearby houses were burned, suffered only superficial impact – its thatched roof merely had bombs embedded in it without detonation, and thanks to strenuous firefighting by the military, only the shrine building was left charred<ref>矢野（2006）：184–185ページ</ref>. However, contracted shrine guards lost their lives in the air raid, and the head priest sustained severe burns<ref name="kg5">矢野（2006）：185ページ</ref>.
Approximately 40 U.S. aircraft formations approached the Inner Shrine as well, but the bombing halted at the mountain on the opposite bank of the [[:en:Isuzu River|Isuzu River]], where anti‑aircraft gun positions<ref name=":1"/> or searchlights<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://tetsukujira.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-1295.html |title=Ise Diary in Wartime – FC2 Version|access-date=2023-10-06|publisher=てっつん}}</ref> were deployed, sparing the Inner Shrine from damage<ref name="kg4"/>. The fact that the Inner Shrine was unharmed was hailed by the priests as a “miracle,” and they wept in gratitude for Ise Grand Shrine’s divine protection<ref name="kg4"/>. Although the guard house of {{ill|Yamato Hime Palace|ja|倭姫宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Hime Palace|qq=}} – a building responsible for transmitting offerings for [[:en:Kagura|Kagura]] and [[:en:Shinsen|Sacred Food]], as well as for conferring [[:en:Jingū taima|Divine Hemp]] and protective charms ([[:en:Omamori|Omamori]]) – was destroyed, the main shrine building remained intact<ref name="kg5"/>. Regarding this, military historian {{ill|Hara Takeshi|ja|原剛 (軍事史家)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hara Takeshi|qq=}} of the [[:en:Ministry of Defense (Japan)|Defense Ministry]] and the {{ill|Defense Research Institute|ja|防衛研究所|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Defense Research Institute|qq=}} explained that by then the U.S. had imposed bombing restrictions on Japanese cultural facilities, with Ise Grand Shrine being specifically mentioned in their guidelines<ref name="mj2"/>.
=== August Air Raids and the End of the War === Even after the massive air raid on [[:en:July 29|July 29]], on the night of [[:en:August 1|August 1]], about 25 B‑29s attacked, and on [[:en:August 14|August 14]], small bombs and [[:en:Strafing|machine gun fire]] were directed at Miyagoto Town and in front of Yamada Station<ref>日本の空襲編集委員会 編（1980）：205, 241ページ</ref>. Then, on [[:en:August 15|August 15]] at noon, the [[:en:Hirohito surrender broadcast|Jewel Voice Broadcast]] was heard, marking Japan’s {{ill|end of the war|ja|終戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/end of the war|qq=}}<ref>三重県歴史教育者協議会 編（2006）：302ページ</ref>. It is said that at Ise Grand Shrine, executives gathered in the main office of the Shrine Administration and, with tears and sobs, listened to the broadcast<ref name="kg1">矢野（2006）：181ページ</ref>. Meanwhile, cannons and other war trophies from the [[:en:Russo-Japanese War|Russo-Japanese War]] that were on display in the shrine grounds were burned overnight by the military using burners and then buried<ref>矢野（2006）：181–182ページ</ref>.
== Post-Air Raid Conditions == [[File:Ise Shrine Geku Sengyo-no-gi 1953.jpg|thumb|250x250px|The first post-war Sengu (Shrine Relocation Ceremony) held in {{ill|1953|ja|1953|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1953|qq=}} (Showa 28)]] [[File:Ise Shrine Geku area Aerial photograph.1983.jpg|thumb|270px|The rebuilt Ise City urban area and Outer Shrine (1983 [Showa 58])<br/><small>{{国土航空写真}}</small>]] After the war, Ise Grand Shrine disassociated itself from [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] and became a {{ill|religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/religious corporation|qq=}}<ref name="sj"/><ref>伊勢文化舎 編（2009）：13ページ</ref>. The Allied forces frequently crossed [[:en:Jeep|jeep]] over Ujibashi, attempting to enter the sacred precincts and troubling the shrine guards<ref>矢野（2006）：188ページ</ref>. Moreover, when an inspection was made by the [[:en:Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|GHQ]], there was a threat that the shrine’s area might be reduced; however, the then-superintendent cleverly argued, “The sacred precincts visible from Ujibashi are essential for nature conservation,” and this was accepted, thus preserving the shrine’s grounds<ref>矢野（2006）：189ページ</ref>. Pilgrimage numbers plummeted – by {{ill|1947|ja|1947|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1947|qq=}} (Showa 22), the number of Outer Shrine pilgrims had dropped to one-tenth of the {{ill|1940|ja|1940|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1940|qq=}} (Showa 15) figures<ref name="sj"/>. This decline has been attributed to social chaos<ref name="nm"/>, as a reaction against pre-war forced pilgrimages<ref name="sj"/>, and also to rumors that military police were detaining pilgrims at Ujibashi and deporting them to {{ill|Okinawa under U.S. administration|ja|アメリカ合衆国による沖縄統治|lt=Okinawa|lt_ja=沖縄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okinawa under U.S. administration|qq=}}<ref name="kg2">矢野（2006）：182ページ</ref>. The Sengu originally scheduled for {{ill|1949|ja|1949|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1949|qq=}} (Showa 24) was postponed in deference to public sentiment and the wishes of [[:en:Hirohito|Emperor Showa]], and with mounting calls to rebuild Ujibashi, reconstruction was undertaken in 1949 (Showa 24), with the postponed 59th Sengu subsequently held four years later in {{ill|1953|ja|1953|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1953|qq=}} (Showa 28)<ref>伊勢文化舎 編（2009）：13–14ページ</ref>. Thereafter, it became customary to rebuild Ujibashi four years before each Sengu ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengyo|qq=}})<ref>伊勢文化舎 編（2009）：14ページ</ref>.
== Air Raid Exhibition Held == In March {{ill|1972|ja|1972|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1972|qq=}} (Showa 47), officials from {{ill|Chiku Rō|ja|地区労|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiku Rō|qq=}} advocated for recording the Ujiyamada Air Raid and submitted a petition titled “Issuance of a Publication Document Recording the Air Raids in Ise City and the Establishment of a Peace Memorial Day.” This petition was adopted by the Ise City Council in January {{ill|1975|ja|1975|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1975|qq=}} (Showa 50)<ref name="jcr">{{Cite web|和書|author=三重県本部伊勢市職|title=戦後五〇年の取り組み|url=https://www.jichiro.gr.jp/jichiken_kako/report/jichikensyo/pdf/3rd_katsudou.pdf|date=1996|accessdate=2015-01-24|archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2015-0124-2116-48/https://www.jichiro.gr.jp:443/jichiken_kako/report/jichikensyo/pdf/3rd_katsudou.pdf|archivedate=2015-01-24}}</ref>. The central figure in this petition, {{ill|Yamakawa Tadazō|ja|山川忠三|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamakawa Tadazō|qq=}}, went on to form the “Association for Recording the Ise City Air Raid,” organizing air raid exhibitions and publishing newsletters detailing the events and personal testimonies<ref name="jcr"/>. Subsequently, the exhibition was held in an organizing committee format, with both Ise City and the Ise City Board of Education as co‑sponsors<ref name="jcr"/>. In {{ill|1988|ja|1988|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1988|qq=}} (Showa 63), the history club of {{ill|Mie Prefectural Ise High School|ja|三重県立伊勢高等学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Ise High School|qq=}} created an incendiary bomb map of Ujiyamada City based on archival materials and interviews, which then became the exhibition’s central display<ref name="jcr"/>. In {{ill|1995|ja|1995|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1995|qq=}} (Heisei 7), marking 50 years since the war, Ise Youth Theater (now known as Gekidan Ise) staged the play “Ise Great Air Raid” on the anniversary of the July 29 air raid<ref name="jcr"/>.
